column1: prompt
You wake up with the ability to hear one lie per day before it's spoken.
The last library on Earth has one empty shelf, and it's slowly filling itself.
Every mirror in your house now shows a five-second delay.
You can only time travel to moments you've forgotten.
A stranger hands you a key that opens any door except the one you actually need.
Your shadow starts arriving a few seconds before you do.
You find a voicemail from yourself, dated tomorrow.
The vending machine only accepts memories as payment.
Every animal in the city stops and looks at you at exactly noon.
You inherit a house where one room exists in yesterday.
Your reflection stopped copying you three days ago, and you're the only one who's noticed.
A text arrives from a number that was disconnected a decade ago.
You can taste other people's memories when you eat something they once loved.
The town's streetlights flicker in Morse code, spelling out tomorrow's headlines.
You find a door in your childhood home that wasn't there before, locked from the other side.
Everyone on Earth falls asleep at the same moment except you.
A letter arrives addressed to you, postmarked fifty years from now.
You realize your dreams are a shared space other people are visiting too.
The new neighbor waters a garden that only grows at night, and only you can see it bloom.
You discover that the anniversary everyone else forgot is the one day a door in town opens.
